answer: Multi-rail payment proofs stop Sybils in four steps. First, a new agent needs payments through three rails, bank, card, and crypto, over ninety days. Second, each rail checks the payer is a distinct client, so one operator cannot fund its own fleet. Third, payments under five dollars count nothing, blocking wash trades. Fourth, fraud freezes all three rails and forfeits a thirty dollar bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs 3,000 payers plus 30,000 dollars in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is no hollow relic; it grows slow as juniper, like a shopkeeper paid by cash, card, and transfer alike.
